cf.title: libpq: Don't read past the end of a message when tracing it

input.subject: libpq: Don't read past the end of a message when tracing it

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducible ASan result, the fix puts the bound in the shared readers of fe-trace.c, and the cost falls only on clients that call PQtrace(). Confidence is medium because no committer has replied and the patch code was not read.

brief.title: libpq: stop PQtrace reading past the end of a message
brief.problem: The protocol tracer in fe-trace.c trusts counts, lengths and string terminators inside server messages, so a malformed message makes a client using PQtrace() read past the message in its input buffer. Messages libpq discards without parsing are read by the tracer alone, so the checks in fe-protocol3.c do not cover them. Security@ judged it not a vulnerability because it needs a hostile server or network.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 passes the end of the message to every reader in fe-trace.c, which stop there and report "mismatched message length: contents exceed length N". It also treats any negative DataRow length as NULL and fixes how CopyBothResponse reads its format count. 0002 stops tracing a pre-3.0 error message during startup, and 0003 adds an AddressSanitizer-oriented TAP test.
user_visible_surface: PQtrace() output: malformed messages are printed as far as they go, with the new note "mismatched message length: contents exceed length N".
PQtrace() output: a DataRow field with any negative length is printed as NULL.
PQtrace() output: a pre-3.0 error message received at connection startup is no longer traced.
New test program libpq_trace_regress and TAP test t/007_trace.pl.
author_claims: Well-formed messages are traced as before; libpq and libpq_pipeline suites pass with unchanged traces.
On master with ASan, 007_trace.pl fails 33 checks with heap-buffer-overflow reports; with the series all 84 pass.
0001's bug dates from v14; 0002's from b8b3f861fbd in v18.
Commitfest 7081 (PQTRACE environment variable) would make these reads easier to reach.
CFBot is green on all platforms.
brief.thread_state: The author pinged after two weeks with no reply. Zsolt Parragi confirmed the series fixes his own fuzzing cases and promised a full review; no committer has replied and back-patching is not decided.
unclear: The thread does not say which branches should get the fix; Alvaro suggested possibly master only.
The thread does not say whether the new trace message text could break tools that parse PQtrace() output.
Including fe-trace.c into a test program is a build pattern a reviewer may need to accept; nobody has commented on it yet.
The AuthenticationMD5Password salt tracing bug is mentioned but not part of this series.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: The series changes how libpq traces received protocol messages, and 0002 skips tracing a pre-3.0 startup error; the protocol itself does not change.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The series closes client-side reads past a message that a hostile server or network can cause; security@ judged it not a vulnerability.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0001's bug dates from v14 and 0002's from v18, and the thread has not decided which branches get the fix.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: 0003 adds the test program libpq_trace_regress, which includes fe-trace.c, and the TAP test t/007_trace.pl.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which branches should get 0001 and 0002: master only, or back to v14 for 0001 and v18 for 0002?
If the series is back-patched, is the new note "mismatched message length: contents exceed length N" acceptable in PQtrace() output on stable branches?
Does 0002 drop the pre-3.0 startup error from the trace entirely, or could the tracer print it in some bounded form?
Is 007_trace.pl useful on builds without AddressSanitizer, or does it only check the printed output there?
Should the series wait for commitfest 7081, or go first and have 7081 rebase onto it?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows libpq's protocol code and fe-trace.c would have to own it. Message #2 Cc's Álvaro, but no committer has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for changed PQtrace() output on malformed messages, the back-patch decision, and a new test program that includes fe-trace.c and must build on all platforms. The liability is small and limited to the tracing code.
committability.author_follow_up: Good signs: the author pinged in message #2, offers to rework or split the series, and promises to rebase onto commitfest 7081 if it lands first.

priority.reason: Only clients that call PQtrace() are affected, but this is a memory-safety fix with an ASan reproduction and an independent confirmation in message #3. The main patch is about 35 KB in one file, fe-trace.c, and the series adds no new user-facing surface beyond one trace note.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claims that every reader stops at the message end and that well-formed traces are unchanged rest on the author's test results. The build pattern of 0003 and the exact trace output for truncated messages need a code-level review.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq trace log
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch began as a libpq client-side query log enabled by connection parameters or environment variables (logdir/PGLOGDIR, logsize/PGLOGSIZE). After review it was narrowed to reworking PQtrace() so it prints one line per protocol message with a timestamp, and enabling it without recompiling was deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Earlier, David Steele moved the patch to PG13 because, in agreement with Andres, it was not clear where the patch was going. The last message before the decision is a review by Alvaro Herrera, who agreed with the one-line-per-message direction but asked for changes. He objected to a frontend_entry[MAXPGPATH] array in pg_conn and listed smaller fixes. The thread shows no new patch or author reply after that review before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This seems to make pg_conn much larger than we'd like.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_tracing
precedents_retrieved.summary: A contrib-style extension, pg_tracing, generates distributed-tracing spans for planner, executor and nested queries, using trace context passed in SQLCommenter comments or a sampling rate. Spans go into a shared memory buffer, and an external forwarder reads them with pg_tracing_consume_spans() and sends them to a trace collector.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas recommended that the author publish pg_tracing as a separate extension on GitHub, and Nikita Malakhov agreed. Heikki's own message is not shown; only the replies quote it. In March 2024 the author said he was moving pg_tracing to a GitHub repository, and the entry was later withdrawn. The visible messages do not show a technical objection that blocked the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: To give a quick update: following Heikki's suggestion, I'm currently working on getting pg_tracing as a separate extension on github.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report tranche ID and LWLock pointer in LWLock static tracepoints
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the LWLock pointer and the numeric tranche ID to each LWLock static tracepoint, so traces can tell individual locks apart and compare them across processes. It also fixes misplaced tracepoints, adds a single tracepoint for all acquires and releases plus start markers for timing, and adds comments on LWLock tranches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Two parts were committed by Peter Eisentraut: the removal of the wrong lwlock__acquire tracepoint in LWLockWaitForVar, and the move of TRACE_POSTGRESQL_LWLOCK_RELEASE. In his last review he reported that patch 0002 did not build on macOS because uint64 was used in the probe definitions, and that the probe changes had no documentation. He also asked for a different argument order and whether both tranche name and tranche ID are needed. The visible messages show no new version after that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
First, a problem:  0002 doesn't build on macOS, because uint64 has been
used in the probe definitions.

Reverted commit(s): libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,
which made the walreceiver non-responsive to SIGTERM while it was
waiting for the connection to be established. That prevented a standby
from being promoted.

Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16
work the same as earlier releases. I reverted it in 'master' too, to
keep the branches in sync. The refactoring was a good idea as such,
but it needs a bit more work. Once we have developed a complete patch
with this issue fixed, let's re-apply that to 'master'.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add new protocol message to change GUCs to be able to change protocol extension parameters
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a protocol message that lets a client set a GUC without a SET command, so poolers can see the change and some parameters can be set only at the protocol level. Over time the work became a patch set with a protocol minor version bump, min_protocol_version and max_protocol_version libpq options, and protocol parameters such as report_parameters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry and moved the remaining protocol patches to the thread about longer cancel keys. Some pieces were committed here, including a libpq function PQfullProtocolVersion added in place of redefining PQprotocolVersion. The visible messages show no objection that rejected the core design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This required another rebase, but I've decided that I think it'll be most fruitful to continue the discussion on protocol changes in the thread about longer cancel keys[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq compression
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds optional compression of libpq protocol traffic between client and server, using zlib or zstd, requested by the client with a connection-string option. Later versions negotiate algorithms through _pq_.compression in the startup packet, wrap compressed data in CompressedData messages, and let a libpq_compression server setting restrict the allowed algorithms and levels.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback because it had been waiting on author for two months. The last author message, in October 2021, promised lz4 support, but no new version followed after Daniel Gustafsson's rebase with a Windows build fix. Earlier review asked for a cleaned-up patch set, a fix for make check-world hangs with zlib, and code cleanup in the shared compression API.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting on author for two months now, so I have
marked it as RwF in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq should append error messages, not overwrite
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed that libpq always append to conn->errorMessage during connection setup and query execution, instead of overwriting it, with only a few defined points that clear it. A second patch labeled each part of the error with the server and port being tried when several hosts are listed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback because the thread had no activity after August and the patch set no longer applied cleanly. Before that, Robert Haas objected that reporting failures from every host adds noise: when the first host is down and the second rejects a password, the user only needs the password error. Tom Lane did not accept this, and the disagreement was not resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The last status of this patch comes from August, which has been
unanswered.  So I am marking the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq compression
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds optional streaming compression of libpq traffic (zlib, LZ4, and ZSTD in a second patch), negotiated through a _pq_.compression startup parameter and the new CompressionAck, CompressedData and SetCompressionMethod messages. A server setting, libpq_compression, controls the allowed algorithms, and each direction of traffic is compressed independently.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jacob Champion marked the entry Returned with Feedback because it had waited on the author for longer than the two-week threshold. The last open review point came from Justin Pryzby in January 2022. He said compression still sat at the layer the 2019 thread had objected to, wrapping secure_read/write through function pointers instead of working inside them, where SSL is handled. The visible messages show no reply from the author to this point. Earlier review also asked for the server setting to default to off for security reasons, and reported an LZ4 assertion failure and CI test failures.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This entry has been waiting on author input for a while (our current threshold is roughly two weeks), so I've marked it Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Libpq Compression
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds protocol-level compression to the wire protocol, on top of a new layered IO stream abstraction that replaces secure_read and secure_write. Client and server announce supported algorithms through the `_pq_.libpq_compression` startup option and a `ParameterStatus` message, and each side then compresses in either direction without further negotiation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after five months without updates, while waiting for the separate discussion on a protocol message to change GUCs. Robert Haas said the user interface was not clear enough to review, citing `libpq_compression=gzip:compress=off` as confusing. He called these UI questions blockers. A reworked syntax with `client_to_server`/`server_to_client` was being discussed when the entry closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I would really like to see this patch go forward, but IMHO these UI questions are blockers.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert no-op changes to BufferGetPage()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert no-op changes to BufferGetPage()
precedents_retrieved.objection:
The reverted changes were intended to force a choice of whether any
newly-added BufferGetPage() calls needed to be accompanied by a
test of the snapshot age, to support the "snapshot too old"
feature.  Such an accompanying test is needed in about 7% of the
cases, where the page is being used as part of a scan rather than
positioning for other purposes (such as DML or vacuuming).  The
additional effort required for back-patching, and the doubt whether
the intended benefit would really be there, have indicated it is
best just to rely on developers to do the right thing based on
comments and existing usage, as we do with many other conventions.

This change should have little or no effect on generated executable
code.

Motivated by the back-patching pain of Tom Lane and Robert Haas

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at the same or a similar idea. The thread mentions only the security@ exchange (message #1), which sent the fix to the normal channels and reports no rejection. It also cites commitfest 7081, a related change to fe-trace.c that the author plans to rebase onto.

Nothing in the user-facing contract breaks: well-formed messages trace as before, and only malformed messages or a pre-3.0 startup error, mainly from out-of-support servers, trace differently. The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump state. A committer may still ask whether the new trace note is acceptable on back branches.

The series has no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL, catalog or replication change. It does not change the wire protocol either; it only changes how libpq prints received messages in PQtrace() output, and the exported PQtrace() API stays the same.

The series closes client-side over-reads of server-controlled data and adds no new privilege, default or exposure. It keeps the trace output within each message, so it reduces what a hostile server can make the client read. Back-patch scope is open, but I found no security failure scenario against the design.

From the maintenance angle this is a contained bugfix and fits core. 0001 puts the bound inside the shared readers (Byte1, Int16, Int32, String, Nchar), so a printer added later for a new message type cannot read past the message even if its author forgets a check. The fix adds no cost for clients that do not trace, adds no GUC, catalog change or dependency, and changes no API. The test program includes fe-trace.c the same way test-oauth-curl.c already includes oauth-curl.c. Changes to the trace output affect only malformed messages, and PQtrace() output is a debugging aid, so tools that parse it are not a reason to keep reading past the buffer. Two points are open but are not objections: which branches get the fix, and the rebase against CF 7081. No committer has replied yet, and Zsolt Parragi's review is still pending.

This is a bug fix in fe-trace.c, and no existing feature or extension stops PQtrace() from reading past a malformed message. The checks in fe-protocol3.c do not cover messages that libpq discards without parsing, and no mechanism is duplicated. The test copies the existing test-oauth-curl.c pattern.

This is a memory-safety bugfix in PQtrace(), not a feature, so the demand test does not apply. Any client that calls PQtrace() is exposed, and Zsolt Parragi found the same reads by fuzzing on his own (message #3).
